Biosphere Theory

Scope, process inventory, and certificate map

The RELIC biosphere domain (relic.scientific.biosphere) represents terrestrial vegetation carbon assimilation, stomatal conductance, autotrophic respiration, organ carbon allocation, structural biomass turnover, leaf phenology, abiotic stress modifiers, and biogenic volatile organic compound (BVOC) synthesis and emission (Methods of Ecological Analysis, Chapters 20–22). Living vegetation is an open, sunlit, metabolically driven subsystem; accordingly, all 23 concrete biosphere Functors inherit BiologicalProcessFunctor and carry Level 1 (read-only constitutive/observation map) or Level 2 (open port/stoichiometric balance) IPHSEquivalenceCertificate declarations. No closed-system Level 4 or Level 5 thermodynamic equilibrium claim is made for living canopy kinetics.

relic.scientific.biosphere.phenology.base.PhenologyBase is an abstract base class shared by the concrete phenology implementations and carries no separate certificate. General notation follows Mathematical Foundations, structural levels follow DEC, IPHS, and GENERIC, and integrator contracts follow Numerical Methods.

Photosynthesis and stomatal conductance

Farquhar-von Caemmerer-Berry biochemical assimilation

relic.scientific.biosphere.photosynthesis.farquhar.FarquharPhotosynthesis (Level 2) implements the \(\mathrm{C_3}\) biochemical model of Farquhar, von Caemmerer, and Berry (1980) with peaked Arrhenius temperature scaling of \(V_{c\max}\), \(J_{\max}\), triose-phosphate utilization \(T_p\), Michaelis constants \(K_c, K_o\), and \(\mathrm{CO}_2\) compensation point \(\Gamma^\ast\) (Bernacchi et al., 2001; Medlyn et al., 2002; Methods of Ecological Analysis, Chapter 20). At intercellular \(\mathrm{CO}_2\) partial pressure or mole fraction \(C_i\) and oxygen level \(O_i\), the Rubisco-limited (\(W_c\)), RuBP-regeneration-limited (\(W_j\)), and TPU-limited (\(W_p\)) gross carboxylation rates are

\[ W_c = V_{c\max}(T_l)\,\frac{C_i}{C_i + K_c(T_l)\left(1 + O_i / K_o(T_l)\right)}, \qquad W_j = \frac{J(I_{\mathrm{APAR}}, T_l)}{4}\,\frac{C_i}{C_i + 2\Gamma^\ast(T_l)}, \qquad W_p = 3\,T_p(T_l)\,\frac{C_i}{C_i - \Gamma^\ast(T_l)}, \]

where electron transport \(J\) solves the non-rectangular hyperbola

\[ \theta_J J^2 - \left(\alpha_J I_{\mathrm{APAR}} + J_{\max}(T_l)\right)J + \alpha_J I_{\mathrm{APAR}} J_{\max}(T_l) = 0 \]

on its smaller positive root. Gross and net leaf or canopy assimilation [\(\mu\)mol \(\mathrm{CO}_2\) m\(^{-2}\) s\(^{-1}\)] satisfy

\[ A_{\mathrm{gross}} = \left(1 - \frac{\Gamma^\ast(T_l)}{C_i}\right)\min_{\mathrm{smooth}}(W_c, W_j, W_p), \qquad A_{\mathrm{net}} = \beta_{\mathrm{stress}}\,A_{\mathrm{gross}} - R_d(T_l), \]

where \(R_d(T_l)\) is mitochondrial day respiration and \(\min_{\mathrm{smooth}}\) denotes quadratic co-limitation (Collatz et al., 1991) or exact pointwise minimum according to configuration.

Optimal stomatal conductance (Medlyn closure)

relic.scientific.biosphere.photosynthesis.stomatal.MedlynStomatalConductance (Level 1) evaluates the optimal water-use-efficiency stomatal conductance law of Medlyn et al. (2011) as a conditional leaf-support observation under the explicit boundary assumption surface_conditions = "leaf_surface_equals_canopy_air". Canopy-ground net assimilation is normalized onto leaf area using leaf_area_index (\(A_{\mathrm{leaf}}\)), leaf-surface \(\mathrm{CO}_2\) is \(C_s\) [\(\mu\)mol mol\(^{-1}\)], and vapor-pressure deficit is bounded away from zero by \(D_{\mathrm{eff}} = \max(D_s, D_{\min})\) [kPa]. Conductance to water vapor \(g_s\) [mol m\(^{-2}\) s\(^{-1}\)] is

\[\begin{split} g_s = \begin{cases} g_0, & \mathrm{PPFD} \le \mathrm{PPFD}_{\mathrm{dark}} \;\text{ or }\; A_{\mathrm{leaf}} \le 0,\\ g_0 + 1.6\left(1 + \dfrac{g_1}{\sqrt{D_{\mathrm{eff}}}}\right)\dfrac{A_{\mathrm{leaf}}}{C_s}, & \mathrm{PPFD} > \mathrm{PPFD}_{\mathrm{dark}} \;\text{ and }\; A_{\mathrm{leaf}} > 0, \end{cases} \end{split}\]

where \(1.6\) is the molecular diffusivity ratio \(D_{\mathrm{H_2O}}/D_{\mathrm{CO_2}}\), \(g_0 \ge 0\) is residual cuticular/minimum conductance, and \(g_1\) [kPa\(^{1/2}\)] is the marginal water-cost slope parameter. MedlynStomatalConductance emits stomatal_conductance via REPLACE without solving an implicit leaf energy balance or mutating carbon pools.

Light-use-efficiency canopy surrogate

relic.scientific.biosphere.surrogates.simple_photosynthesis.SimpleCanopyPhotosynthesis (Level 2) provides a diagnostic Monteith (1972) light-use-efficiency closure,

\[ \mathrm{GPP} = \varepsilon_{\max}\,\mathrm{APAR}\,f_T(T_a)\,f_{\mathrm{VPD}}(D)\,\beta_W, \]

for coarse-scale or calibration workflows where biochemical \(C_i\) iteration is not selected. Exactly one photosynthesis owner (FarquharPhotosynthesis or SimpleCanopyPhotosynthesis) may own gpp in a given simulator graph.

Autotrophic respiration, allocation, and structural growth

Maintenance, growth, and total autotrophic respiration

RELIC separates autotrophic respiration into modular Level 2 owners (Methods of Ecological Analysis, Chapter 21; Ryan, 1991; Amthor, 2000):

  1. relic.scientific.biosphere.respiration.maintenance_respiration.MaintenanceRespiration evaluates organ-summed maintenance cost from live biomass \(C_k\) or tissue nitrogen content \(N_k\) with \(Q_{10}\) or modified-Arrhenius temperature acclimation (Atkin and Tjoelker, 2003):

    \[R_m = \sum_{k \in \{\mathrm{leaf,stem,root}\}} r_{m,k}\,M_k\,f_{T,k}(T_k), \qquad f_{T,k}(T_k) = Q_{10,k}^{(T_k - T_{\mathrm{ref}})/10}.\]

  2. relic.scientific.biosphere.respiration.growth_respiration.GrowthRespiration computes biosynthetic construction cost on positive net assimilatory surplus:

    \[R_g = f_{\mathrm{gr}}\,\max(\mathrm{GPP} - R_m,\; 0), \qquad 0 \le f_{\mathrm{gr}} < 1.\]

  3. relic.scientific.biosphere.respiration.autotrophic_respiration.AutotrophicRespiration closes the canopy autotrophic carbon flux budget:

    \[R_a = R_m + R_g, \qquad \mathrm{NPP} = \mathrm{GPP} - R_a, \qquad \mathrm{CUE} = \frac{\mathrm{NPP}}{\max(\mathrm{GPP}, \varepsilon_{\mathrm{GPP}})}.\]

Simplex carbon allocation and organ mass conservation

relic.scientific.biosphere.growth.biomass_allocation.BiomassAllocation (Level 2) maps environmental light, water, and nutrient limitation signals to organ allocation fractions \(\mathbf{a} = (a_{\mathrm{leaf}}, a_{\mathrm{stem}}, a_{\mathrm{root}})^{\mathsf{T}}\) (Friedlingstein et al., 1999) satisfying exact simplex normalization:

\[ a_k \ge 0, \qquad \sum_{k \in \{\mathrm{leaf,stem,root}\}} a_k = 1, \qquad F_{\mathrm{alloc},k} = a_k\,\max(\mathrm{NPP}, 0). \]

relic.scientific.biosphere.growth.structural_growth.StructuralGrowth (Level 2) advances organ carbon pools \(C_k\) [g C m\(^{-2}\)] with senescence turnover rates \(\tau_k^{-1}\):

\[ \frac{\mathrm{d}C_k}{\mathrm{d}t} = F_{\mathrm{alloc},k} - L_k, \qquad L_k = \frac{C_k}{\tau_k}\,f_{\mathrm{sen},k}, \]

emitting integrated pool increments \(\Delta C_k\) via UpdateItem(ACCUMULATE, per_timestep=True), litterfall fluxes \(L_k\) (REPLACE, routed to pedosphere LitterfallInterfaceMapper), and prognostic leaf area index \(L_{\mathrm{AI}} = \mathrm{SLA}\cdot C_{\mathrm{leaf}}\) so the step carbon ledger \(\sum_k \Delta C_k + \sum_k L_k\Delta t - \sum_k F_{\mathrm{alloc},k}\Delta t = 0\) closes identically. relic.scientific.biosphere.growth.phenology_growth.PhenologyGrowth (Level 1) supplies read-only stage-dependent growth multipliers without mutating carbon stocks.

Phenology and abiotic stress closures

Leaf phenology models

Concrete phenology Functors inherit relic.scientific.biosphere.phenology.base.PhenologyBase:

  • StaticPhenology (Level 2): emits prescribed stationary \(L_{\mathrm{AI}}\) and greenness fraction.

  • GDDPhenology (Level 2): accumulates daily thermal forcing \(\Delta \mathrm{GDD} = \max(T_a - T_{\mathrm{base}}, 0)\,\Delta t_{\mathrm{days}}\) (ACCUMULATE, per_timestep=True) to drive logistic budburst, full-canopy plateau, and cold/photoperiod senescence.

  • GSIPhenology (Level 2): evaluates the Jolly et al. (2005) Growing Season Index as the product of piecewise-linear minimum-temperature, photoperiod, and vapor-pressure-deficit indicators, \(\mathrm{GSI} = i_{T_{\min}}\,i_{\mathrm{photo}}\,i_{\mathrm{VPD}} \in [0, 1]\).

  • CropPhenology (Level 2): tracks vernalization- and photoperiod-weighted thermal units across emergence, vegetative, flowering, grain-filling, and maturity stages (ACCUMULATE thermal progress, REPLACE stage diagnostics).

  • PhenologyFunctor (Level 1): projects active phenological stage indices and canopy-activity scalars without owning separate carbon storage.

Water, nutrient, thermal, and ozone stress Functors

WaterStress, NutrientStress, and ThermalStress (Level 1) are pure constitutive observers mapping soil water content or potential, foliar N and P ratios, and leaf temperature extremes to bounded dimensionless scalars \(\beta_W, \beta_N, \beta_T \in [0, 1]\) (REPLACE).

relic.scientific.biosphere.stress.ozone_stress.OzoneStress (Level 2) integrates phytotoxic ozone dose above flux threshold \(y\) (\(\mathrm{POD}_y\), [mmol m\(^{-2}\)]; Emberson et al., 2000; Sitch et al., 2007):

\[ F_{\mathrm{O_3,stom}} = g_{s,\mathrm{O_3}}\,[\mathrm{O}_3]_{\mathrm{canopy}}, \qquad \Delta \mathrm{POD}_y = \max\!\left(F_{\mathrm{O_3,stom}} - y,\; 0\right)\Delta t, \]

committing \(\Delta \mathrm{POD}_y\) via UpdateItem(ACCUMULATE, per_timestep=True) and emitting the resulting photosynthetic damage factor \(\beta_{\mathrm{O_3}} = \operatorname{clip}(1 - a_{\mathrm{O_3}}\,\mathrm{POD}_y,\; \beta_{\mathrm{O_3,min}},\; 1)\) via REPLACE.

Biogenic volatile organic compound (BVOC) synthesis and emission

Canopy empirical MEGAN closure and continuous CO2 inhibition

relic.scientific.biosphere.bvoc.megan_model.MEGANModel (Level 2) evaluates canopy BVOC emission rate \(E_s\) for compound class \(s\) following Guenther et al. (2006, 2012) (Methods of Ecological Analysis, Chapter 22):

\[ E_s = \varepsilon_s\,\gamma_{\mathrm{CE}}(L_{\mathrm{AI}})\,\gamma_P(\mathrm{PPFD})\,\gamma_T(T_l)\,\gamma_{\mathrm{age}}\,\gamma_{\mathrm{SM}}(\theta)\,\gamma_{\mathrm{CO_2}}(C_a), \]

where \(\varepsilon_s\) is the standard-condition emission factor and \(\gamma_{\mathrm{CE}}, \gamma_P, \gamma_T, \gamma_{\mathrm{age}}, \gamma_{\mathrm{SM}}\) are the canopy-environment, light, temperature-optimum, leaf-age, and soil-moisture activity factors. For isoprene \(\mathrm{CO}_2\) inhibition, RELIC evaluates the Wilkinson et al. (2009) / Guenther et al. (2012, Eq. 14) Hill curve continuously from intercellular concentration \(C_i = r_{C_i} C_a\) (\(r_{C_i} = 0.7\), so \(C_i = 280\) ppm at \(C_a = 400\) ppm):

\[ \gamma_{\mathrm{CO_2}}(C_a) = \mathrm{IS}_{\max} - \frac{\mathrm{IS}_{\max}\,C_i^h}{C_\ast^h + C_i^h}, \]

with \(\mathrm{IS}_{\max} = 1.344\), \(C_\ast = 585\) ppm, and \(h = 1.4614\). At ambient \(C_a = 400\) ppm, this continuous parameterization evaluates to 1.0024713532535012 in float64 (1.0024713277816772 in float32); RELIC does not apply an ad-hoc discontinuity clamp forcing \(\gamma_{\mathrm{CO_2}}(400\;\mathrm{ppm}) = 1\).

Mechanistic plastidic isoprene, resin-pool monoterpene, and sesquiterpene synthesis

  1. Plastidic MEP isoprene synthesis (IsopreneSynthesis, Level 2): relic.scientific.biosphere.bvoc.synthesis.isoprene.IsopreneSynthesis models chloroplastic dimethylallyl diphosphate (DMADP) supply driven by photosynthetic electron transport \(J\) and ATP/NADPH energetic availability (Niinemets et al., 1999; Morfopoulos et al., 2014), coupled with isoprene synthase Arrhenius kinetics. Without a permanent leaf storage organ, emission equals instantaneous enzymatic synthesis (REPLACE).

  2. Dual de-novo and bounded storage-pool monoterpene dynamics (MonoterpeneSynthesis, Level 2): relic.scientific.biosphere.bvoc.synthesis.monoterpene.MonoterpeneSynthesis separates light-dependent de novo synthesis \(S_{\mathrm{denovo}}\) from a specialized resin-duct or glandular-trichome storage pool \(P \in [0, P_{\max}]\) (Schurgers et al., 2009; Grote et al., 2013). With storage-directed synthesis \(S_{\mathrm{pool}}\) and temperature-driven volatilization release \(E_{\mathrm{pool}} = k_{\mathrm{rel}}(T_l)\,P\), raw storage advancement \(P_{\mathrm{raw}} = P + (S_{\mathrm{pool}} - E_{\mathrm{pool}})\Delta t\) is projected onto \([0, P_{\max}]\):

    \[P_{\mathrm{next}} = \operatorname{clip}(P_{\mathrm{raw}},\; 0,\; P_{\max}), \qquad r_{\mathrm{bound}} = \frac{P_{\mathrm{raw}} - P_{\mathrm{next}}}{\Delta t},\]

    committing \(\Delta P = P_{\mathrm{next}} - P\) via UpdateItem(ACCUMULATE, per_timestep=True) and recording any capacity-clamp flux explicitly in pool_boundary_residual_rate (\(r_{\mathrm{bound}}\)) so the terpene carbon ledger closes identically:

    \[\frac{\Delta P}{\Delta t} + E_{\mathrm{pool}} + r_{\mathrm{bound}} - S_{\mathrm{pool}} = 0.\]

  3. Stress-induced sesquiterpene synthesis (SesquiterpeneStressModel Level 1, SesquiterpeneSynthesis Level 2): relic.scientific.biosphere.bvoc.synthesis.sesquiterpene.SesquiterpeneStressModel (Level 1) aggregates oxidative, thermal, and biotic/mechanical stress cues into a non-negative induction multiplier \(\gamma_{\mathrm{stress}}\) (REPLACE), which relic.scientific.biosphere.bvoc.synthesis.sesquiterpene.SesquiterpeneSynthesis (Level 2) combines with \(\beta\)-exponential temperature volatility \(\exp(\beta_{\mathrm{SQT}}(T_l - T_s))\) and light-modulated de novo farnesyl-diphosphate synthesis (Duhl et al., 2008).

In composed graphs, users select either canopy empirical MEGANModel or the mechanistic compound synthesis owners for a given BVOC flux target so surface emissions to atmospheric chemistry and observation operators have a single writer.

References

  • Amthor, J. S. (2000). The McCree-de Wit-Penning de Vries-Thornley respiration paradigms: 30 years later. Annals of Botany, 86, 1-20.

  • Atkin, O. K. and Tjoelker, M. G. (2003). Thermal acclimation and the dynamic response of plant respiration to temperature. Trends in Plant Science, 8, 343-351.

  • Bernacchi, C. J., Singsaas, E. L., Pimentel, C., Portis, A. R., and Long, S. P. (2001). Improved temperature response functions for models of Rubisco-limited photosynthesis. Plant, Cell & Environment, 24, 253-259.

  • Collatz, G. J., Ball, J. T., Grivet, C., and Berry, J. A. (1991). Physiological and environmental regulation of stomatal conductance, photosynthesis and transpiration: a model that includes a laminar boundary layer. Agricultural and Forest Meteorology, 54, 107-136.
